2026-08-20T12:30:57.6213830Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6214226Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6214552Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6215045Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6215622Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6216134Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6217986Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6219765Z >
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6222041Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6224431Z >
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6225229Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6225958Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6226150Z ### How to Use
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6226386Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6284603Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6285742Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6285971Z ```bash
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6286680Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6287909Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6288539Z ```
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6288748Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6289034Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6289574Z ```bash
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6290456Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6291257Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6293600Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6294977Z ```
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6295186Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6295874Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6297710Z ```bash
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6298300Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6299088Z ```
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6299308Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6299677Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6300528Z ```bash
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6301069Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6301929Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6302629Z ```
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6302843Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6303112Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6303519Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6304915Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6306470Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6306651Z ```bash
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6307103Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6308162Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6308986Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6309301Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6309795Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6310799Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6311611Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6312125Z ```
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6312338Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6313073Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6313942Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6314127Z ```bash
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6314815Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6315691Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6316397Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6316829Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6317396Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6318205Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6325589Z ```
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6325981Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6326229Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6327374Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6328379Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6329358Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6330360Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6331570Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6332094Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6332272Z ### Notes
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6332498Z 
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6333127Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6334657Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6335885Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6337113Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6338466Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6339623Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6340599Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-20T12:30:57.6341318Z </mcp-clis>
